label: TP
reason: Both alerts are True Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss): User input flows from getParameter() through doSomething() -> bar -> SQL string -> response.getWriter().println(), reaching the HTML sink at lines 54-57. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): Same user input reaches the SQL query string at line 51 ('PASSWORD=' + bar + ''') without parameterization. Despite encodeForHTML() appearing later in the code, it encodes the already-built SQL string for display purposes only—not for preventing SQL injection during database execution.
